newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa - Bebear says 65 "reasonable age" to retire.
newsitem.headline: Axa - Bebear says 65 "reasonable age" to retire.

text.p: Axa-UAP chairman Claude Bebear said on Wednesday that 65 was a good age to retire but did not commit himself to stepping down then.
Asked at a news conference about his retirement plans, Bebear, who will be 62 next July, replied, "We will see."
Bebear said, however, that he did not "plan to stay on indefinitely. Sixty-five is a totally reasonable (age to retire)."
He said he had no worries about finding a successor, saying the biggest problem was an abundance of talent in the ranks.

"There's a wide range of individuals capable of succeeding me," he told the news conference, pointing to the row of Axa-UAP executives. The news conference was held to announce the group's 1996 results.
Bebear said last year he had decided to work only four days a week.
Analysts said that they expected Bebear to want to oversee and consolidate the merger of Axa-UAP before retiring. That is expected to take several years at least.
